title: Yash's ₹800-Crore 'Toxic' Just Got Delayed Again — and the Global Strategy Behind It Tells You Everything
excerpt: The most expensive Indian film ever made keeps pushing its release date. The reason? It's not being built for India alone.
body:
Yash doesn't do small. The man who turned a Kannada-language gangster saga into a ₹1,200-crore global phenomenon with *KGF* has been plotting something even more audacious — and the wait just got longer.

*Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups*, the period gangster epic that's been described as the most expensive Indian film ever produced, has been delayed yet again. Originally slated for March 19, 2026, then pushed to June, the film now appears headed for an August window. For the lakhs of NRI fans who've been refreshing BookMyShow and AMC showtimes for months, this is starting to feel personal.

## Why the Delays Keep Piling Up

Director Geetu Mohandas — the acclaimed Malayalam filmmaker making her big-budget debut — isn't rushing. The film, budgeted at a staggering ₹700–800 crore, is being shot simultaneously in Kannada and English, with dubbed versions planned in Hindi, Telugu, Tamil, and Malayalam. That alone would make the logistics nightmarish. But the real complexity lies in global distribution.

"We need to finish the film completely before we update the release," Yash said recently, emphasising that *Toxic* isn't just an Indian movie — it's engineered for a worldwide rollout. Action choreography by J.J. Perry (who directed *John Wick: Chapter 4*'s stunts) and VFX by DNEG (the studio behind *Oppenheimer* and *Dune*) suggest Hollywood-grade ambitions.

Then there's the exhibition politics. Exhibitors have pushed back against a "clubbing deal" that would bundle *Toxic* with *Dhurandhar 2*, and a religious controversy over cemetery scenes added a legal wrinkle the production didn't need. Each delay has compounded into the next.

## CinemaCon Changed the Conversation

Here's the twist: every delay is also building anticipation. At CinemaCon 2026, a nine-minute preview left international distributors "speechless," according to trade reports. Set across the 1940s through 1970s in Goa, the film casts Yash in a dual role opposite Kiara Advani, Nayanthara, and Huma Qureshi — a lineup that spans four of India's biggest film industries.

IMAX has confirmed *Toxic* for its 2026 premium slate alongside Ranbir Kapoor's *Ramayana*, positioning it as a genuine event film rather than a standard release.

## The Diaspora Is Watching

For NRIs, *Toxic* represents something unusual: an Indian film designed from the ground up for the international market. The English-language track means it won't rely solely on subtitled screenings in multiplex chains. Yash's popularity already crosses regional lines — the *KGF* franchise grossed over $50 million internationally — and *Toxic* is clearly calibrated to expand that footprint.

The delays are frustrating, but they also signal confidence. You don't push back an ₹800-crore film unless you believe the global window matters more than rushing to fill a domestic slot.

## What's Next

The August 2026 date is the current bet, though nothing has been officially locked. The first single, *Tabaahi* (featuring Yash and Kiara Advani), dropped in March and has already crossed 100 million views on YouTube. The marketing machine is running. The film just isn't — yet.

If *Toxic* delivers on even half the CinemaCon promise, the wait will have been worth it. If it doesn't, ₹800 crore is a very expensive fairy tale.
